zero_omission_notes.summary: Covers geometric similarity, Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem) and its converse, and criteria for triangle similarity (AAA, SSS, SAS).

detailed_sections.full_explanation: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: BPT (Thales Theorem)
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: In ΔABC, if DE || BC, then AD/DB = AE/EC.

detailed_sections.full_explanation: AAA, SSS, SAS criteria for ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. Corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: AA Similarity Criterion
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, triangles are similar.

short_answer_questions.question: State and prove BPT theorem statement.
short_answer_questions.answer: Statement: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle, it divides the other two sides in the same ratio. Proof uses area ratio of triangles with common heights.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Diagonals of trapezium ABCD with AB || DC intersect at O. Show AO/BO = CO/DO.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: In ΔAOB and ΔCOD: ∠OAB = ∠OCD, ∠OBA = ∠ODC (alternate interior). ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD (AA) => AO/CO = BO/DO => AO/BO = CO/DO.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: If a line intersects sides AB and AC of ΔABC at D and E respectively and is parallel to BC, prove AD/AB = AE/AC.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Since DE || BC, AD/DB = AE/EC by BPT. Taking reciprocals: DB/AD = EC/AE. Adding 1 to both sides: (DB+AD)/AD = (EC+AE)/AE => AB/AD = AC/AE. Inverting back: AD/AB = AE/AC.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: Girl height 90 cm walks away from lamp-post (height 3.6 m) at speed 1.2 m/s.

qa.question: Find length of her shadow after 4 seconds.
qa.answer: Distance walked = 1.2 * 4 = 4.8 m. By similar triangles: x / (x + 4.8) = 0.9 / 3.6 = 1/4 => 4x = x + 4.8 => 3x = 4.8 => x = 1.6 m.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Listing vertices out of order when stating triangle similarity.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Always maintain exact corresponding vertex order: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF.
